The concept of "mutual coercion, mutually agreed upon" refers to the idea that countries
can collectively agree to impose sanctions on one another to address global climate change
effectively. By establishing a framework where all countries participate in creating
enforceable sanctions, the incentive structure surrounding carbon emissions and
environmental responsibility can be transformed. For example, nations might agree to
impose tariffs on goods from countries that do not meet specified emissions targets,
thereby encouraging compliance through economic consequences. This collaborative approach
ensures that all parties are held accountable, fostering a shared commitment to reducing
greenhouse gas emissions and promoting sustainable practices. Ultimately, such mutual
coercion can lead to more significant progress in combating climate change by aligning
national interests with global environmental goals.
